corrections.claimed_speedup: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks data.json of 2026-09-24 (commit f673364), GET /: Drogon 1.9 126,432 / 134,984 / 131,608 req/s at concurrency 64 / 256 / 512 vs Go net/http ('nethttp', label 1.22) 71,499 / 67,382 / 67,239 req/s, i.e. 1.77x / 2.00x / 1.96x (derived from page data)
corrections.workload: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks (develop branch, run of 2026-09-24): GET / (empty body) for 15 s at each concurrency level 64/256/512, generated by zrk --closed (closed loop over keep-alive connections), not oha. The framework container is pinned to cores 0-3 (SERVER_CPUS) and the load generator to cores 4-15; every Drogon, oatpp and nethttp run in this snapshot reports server_cpu_saturation of about 0.99 on about 3.95 cores (server-bound, valid by the suite's own probe).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: debian:trixie-slim + build-essential (Debian trixie default gcc/g++ is GCC 14.2; the suite does not print the version). Drogon v1.9.13 is built through add_subdirectory with `cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=release` (cpp/drogon/config.yaml), so CMake Release flags apply (-O3 -DNDEBUG by default for GCC); C++17. Go side: golang:1.27 image, `go build -trimpath`, GOAMD64=v3 on amd64.
corrections.hardware: Single shared host per data.json metadata: 16 CPUs, 7.7 GB RAM (7733008 kB), Linux 7.2.6-200.fc44.x86_64. cpu_name reads 'M1 Eight-Core Processor', which contradicts x86_64, so the CPU model is unknown (a comment in the suite's go/Dockerfile names an AMD Ryzen 7 5700U host; not confirmed for this run). Server container limited to 4 cores (SERVER_CPUS=0-3); load generator on the other 12.
corrections.caveats: Numbers come from the develop-branch data.json of 2026-09-24 (the zrk --closed keep-alive method adopted in September 2026). data.json is overwritten on every run, and the suite says runs from different benchmark revisions are not comparable. The master-branch data.json (2026-09-20, earlier zrk ramp method) shows a smaller gap: Drogon 120,197 / 101,786 / 101,282 vs nethttp 96,149 / 85,406 / 83,964 req/s (about 1.2x). Hello-world endpoint only, server pinned to 4 cores; the CPU label in data.json is garbled. A separate single-author benchmark (gonwan/webframework-benchmark, 0 stars, AMD 7840HS host, wrk with keep-alive) shows Drogon 1.8.7 at 320k/s vs Boost.Beast 1.83 at 220k/s, with nginx at 336k/s.

notes: The record's numbers match the develop-branch data.json (default branch, commit f673364), not the master URL it cited, where Drogon leads nethttp by only about 1.2x under the older method; benchmark_url is now pinned to that commit. The run used zrk with keep-alive, not oha, and the build is CMake release, not unflagged. Metadata (MIT, 14,303 stars, last commit 2026-09-16, not a fork) verified.
